prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Conservative Party Manifesto 2017 – Summary (under 500 words)

Vision and approach
- Deliver “strong and stable” leadership through Brexit, tackle five “giant challenges”: a strong economy; Brexit and a changing world; enduring social divisions; an ageing society; and fast-changing technology.
- Govern from the mainstream, value the good government can do, and focus on ordinary working families.
- Build a “Great Meritocracy” with opportunity based on talent and effort, not background.

Economy and business
- Maintain sound public finances, low taxes, simplified tax system; raise personal allowance to £12,500 and higher rate to £50,000 by 2020; no VAT rise; cut corporation tax to 17%.
- Reform business rates; reduce red tape; update regulation (utilities, transport) to improve consumer value.
- Support free trade: secure a deep UK-EU partnership; replicate existing EU FTAs; create Trade Commissioners and reconvene the Board of Trade.
- Workers: raise National Living Wage to 60% of median by 2020, then by median earnings; act on gig economy protections (post-Taylor Review); crack down on tax evasion.
- Corporate governance: binding annual votes on executive pay; publish pay ratios; employee voice on boards; enforce takeover promises; protect pensions; scrutinise foreign ownership of critical infrastructure.

Industrial strategy and infrastructure
- Increase R&D to 2.4% of GDP within 10 years (aim 3% long-term); grow university investment funds.
- £23bn National Productivity Investment Fund for housing, R&D, infrastructure and skills.
- Back key sectors (auto, aero, life sciences, digital, creative), SMEs, prompt payment; review energy costs and deliver competitive prices.
- Energy: diverse mix; lead in offshore wind; develop UK shale with strong regulation and community benefit.
- Transport: proceed with HS2, Northern Powerhouse Rail, Heathrow expansion; expand road/rail capacity; support EVs (aim near-zero emission fleet by 2050).

Stronger communities and Union
- Spread growth via devolution deals, local industrial strategies, cultural investment; improve urban design, air quality, and green spaces.
- Rural: maintain farm support cash until 2022; new agri-environment system next parliament; enhance animal welfare; safeguard post offices.
- Coastal: extend Coastal Communities Fund; new post-CFP fisheries regime.
- Union: oppose a second Scottish independence referendum “now”; new growth deals (Borderlands, North Wales); move civil service and Channel 4 functions out of London; create a UK Shared Prosperity Fund from returned EU funds.

Brexit and Global Britain
- Leave single market and customs union; seek comprehensive FTA/customs agreement; Great Repeal Bill converts EU law; protect workers’ rights; maintain CTA with Ireland; “no deal better than a bad deal.”
- Maintain 0.7% aid (with reform of definitions if needed); champion free trade, climate action, girls’ education, and fight modern slavery.

Security, defence and justice
- Meet NATO 2% and increase defence spending 0.5% above inflation annually; retain Trident; invest £178bn in equipment; support veterans.
- Policing: create national infrastructure police; fold SFO into NCA; expand cyber security; strengthen counter-terrorism.
- Justice: victims’ law, extend unduly lenient sentence scheme; modernise courts; reform prisons (10,000 places), community sentences focused on rehabilitation.

Meritocracy and society
- Schools: expand free schools; allow new selective schools with conditions; involve universities/independent schools in state sector; fairer funding with £4bn more by 2022; replace universal infant lunches with free breakfasts; EBacc targets; teacher support and retention.
- Technical education: introduce T-levels, more hours, mandatory placements; create institutes of technology; 3m apprenticeships; adult retraining and digital lifelong learning.
- Immigration: reduce net migration to “tens of thousands”; tougher family/student visa rules; control EU migration post-Brexit.
- Equalities and health: close gender and ethnicity pay gaps; new Mental Health Bill; 10,000 more mental health staff; raise disability employment by 1m; Domestic Violence and Abuse Bill; halve rough sleeping by 2022, end by 2027.
- Consumers and cost of living: stronger regulators; fairer rail, telecoms, leasehold; energy safeguard tariff cap; smart meters for all by 2020; energy efficiency push; “Breathing Space” for problem debt.

Intergenerational contract, NHS, and care
- Balance the budget by mid-2020s; state pension “triple lock” until 2020 then “double lock”; review state pension age with life expectancy.
- Social care: include home value in domiciliary means test; £100,000 asset floor; extend deferred payments; consult on system improvements; means-test Winter Fuel Payments; other pensioner benefits maintained.
- NHS: minimum £8bn real-terms rise over five years; expand training; major capital programme; recover overseas treatment costs; faster access to new drugs; support 7-day services; retain A&E 95% and 18-week targets; improve cancer, mental health, learning disability and end-of-life care.

Digital age
- Digital Charter: make UK best to start/run digital business and safest online.
- Infrastructure: universal high-speed by 2020; more full fibre, 5G majority coverage by 2027; better rail/road connectivity and WiFi.
- Data and safety: new data protection law; right to delete data at 18; Data Use and Ethics Commission; levy on platforms to counter harms; tougher duties on platforms re harmful/terror content; online child safety and education.
- Government: digital-by-default services, Verify rollout, open data; create a geospatial data body; repeal Leveson 2 and Section 40.
